snippets.rationale: These destructive Stack fixture commands require an explicit operator kubeconfig and are described, not run by the docs gate.
Starting the local Stack creates disposable infrastructure and needs the operator's already-running OrbStack cluster.
Parallel Stack commands intentionally create named local infrastructure and must only run under an operator-owned kubeconfig.
The Tilt command is an interactive development operation that requires a local Kubernetes context and is not safe for docs CI.
The containment proof provisions a disposable cluster and writes evidence to an operator-selected path, so CI does not execute it as a snippet.
Status inspection depends on an existing local Stack selected by the operator and has no standalone deterministic fixture.
Reset and teardown intentionally mutate a named local Stack and are never executed merely because documentation changed.
This is an explanatory data-flow diagram rather than a command or source sample that CI can execute.
The command starts a user-selected local API and therefore receives deterministic shell parsing rather than automatic execution.
This is a terminal command grammar explaining interactive input, not a shell command that an unattended CI process can execute.
The command starts a loopback web server and is syntax-checked without binding a port during documentation CI.
This is an explanatory lifecycle sequence rather than a command or compilable code sample.
The local API command is shell-checked; starting it requires deliberate local credentials and a long-running process fixture.
This object fragment is parsed as JSON by the docs gate to catch malformed configuration syntax without changing configuration.
The API tutorial command is parsed as POSIX shell; executing it needs operator-supplied local credentials and a controlled process lifecycle.
The web tutorial starts a loopback server, so the docs gate verifies syntax without starting or retaining an interactive process.
The terminal tutorial is syntax-checked; executing it requires a separately started local runtime and interactive user input.
The local API command is parsed as POSIX shell; executing it requires deliberate local credentials and a controlled process lifecycle.
The web inbox starts a loopback server, so documentation CI verifies syntax without binding a port or retaining an interactive process.
The terminal inbox requires a separately started local runtime and interactive input, so the docs gate checks deterministic shell syntax only.
